payload.question:
## Context

Confirmed by research (docs/history/submit-dependency-scan-delivered-blindspot/RESEARCH.md): `fgos list`'s default view (bin/fgos.mjs:2647-2660) filters out any item where `isResolvedStatus(item)` is true (src/state/frontier.mjs:266, TAIL_RESOLVED_STATUSES at line 244 = delivered/retrospective/cleanup/done), unless `--all` is passed. `plugins/fgOS/skills/submit/SKILL.md:65-71` step 2's dependency-candidate scan calls exactly `list --json`, no `--all`, so a `delivered`-but-not-yet-`cleanup` item is invisible to duplicate detection -- this is the confirmed root cause of the tsk-17m/tsk-1dd collision cited in the item description. Precedent check: `herdr-plugin/src/fgos.rs`'s 3 call sites always use `list --all --json` when a complete cross-status picture is needed -- the one other consumer in this repo with a similar need already widens rather than staying narrow.

## Why this matters

The item itself proposes 3 options and explicitly does not prescribe one ("Required decision... not prescribing one"). Research found no repo evidence that settles this mechanically: Option 1 (widen the scan) has precedent (herdr-plugin's `--all` usage) but itself splits into an unresolved sub-choice -- bare `--all` (also catches `done`/`wontfix` duplicates, which may be desirable, but pulls in the largest working set) vs. a narrower delivered/retrospective/cleanup-only filter (matches the item's stated root cause exactly, but is new filter logic with no existing precedent in this codebase). Option 2 (document only) and Option 3 (dedicated recency check) have no supporting or disqualifying evidence either. Which option to build -- and, if Option 1, how wide the filter should be -- is a scope decision, not a fact this stage can resolve alone; a person needs to pick a direction before planning can proceed.
